title: I'm from Indonesia
title_target: Я з Індонезії — Ya z Indoneziyi
goal: Say which country and city you're from, ask where others are from, and say which languages you speak — while meeting the second case (родовий, the genitive) through its busiest doorway: the preposition з.
bekal: put country and city names into the родовий
choose between з, із, and зі
say nationalities for men and women

dialogs.title: Діалог — In the university corridor
dialogs.intro: Andriy says hi to Ani before class starts. Notice that a country's name changes its ending every time it follows з — Індонезія becomes Індонезії, Україна becomes України.

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: Nice to meet you. I'm Andriy. Where are you from?
lines.literal: very — pleasant. I — Andriy. where-from — you?

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: Very far. And where are you from?

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: I'm from Ukraine, from Lviv. But right now I live in Kyiv.
lines.literal: I — from — Ukraine, from — Lviv. but — now — I — live — in — Kyiv.

lines.speaker: Андрій:
lines.id: A little. And do you speak Ukrainian?

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: Not yet. Only a little. I'm learning Ukrainian.
lines.literal: still — no. only — a-little. I — study — Ukrainian.

notes: **Звідки asks where you're from, not where you are.** *Звідки ти?* = where are you from? *Де ти?* = where are you (right now)? Two different questions, answered with different cases. Compare: *Я з України* (origin) vs *Я в Україні* (where I am now).

**After з, a country's name goes into the родовий.** The good news is that the pattern is very tidy for countries ending in **-я**: Індонезія → **Індонезії**, Японія → **Японії**, Малайзія → **Малайзії**. Countries ending in **-а** switch to **-и**: Україна → **України**, Канада → **Канади**, Америка → **Америки**.

**з, із, зі — one word in three outfits.** The choice is purely about what's easy to say. **з** before a vowel or a single consonant (*з Києва*), **із** before a cluster of consonants (*із Сінгапуру*), **зі** before a cluster starting with с/з/ш/ж (*зі Львова*, *зі школи*). ⚠️ Picking the wrong one doesn't change the meaning and everyone still understands — so don't let it stop you talking.

**Languages use the -ською form, not the language's name.** *Я говорю українською* is literally "I speak in-the-Ukrainian-way". This form is the fifth case (орудний, the instrumental), but you don't need to know that yet — just remember the ending **-ською** or **-цькою**.

**But when the language is the thing being studied, the ending changes.** *Я вивчаю українську* (I'm learning Ukrainian) — here the language is the object of the action, and the ending is **-ську**. Compare in pairs: *говорю українською* / *вивчаю українську*.

**Ще ні = not yet.** Literally "still no". It's a much softer answer than a bare *ні*, and very useful for beginners: it admits your limits while signaling that you're working on it. The opposite is **вже** (already).

**Ukrainian city names come from Ukrainian itself.** Київ (Kyiv), Львів (Lviv), Харків (Kharkiv), Одеса (Odesa), Дніпро (Dnipro). ⚠️ The forms *Киев*, *Львов*, *Одесса* are Russian spellings; using them in Ukraine sounds like calling a country by its old colonial name.

grammars.title: Звідки? — origin, with з + родовий
body: Watch the pattern, not the individual words. The ending **-а** becomes **-и**; **-я** becomes **-ї**; a consonant gets **-у** or **-а**.

grammars.title: Languages: говорити + the -ською ending
body: One formula, any language. Stick **-ською** (or **-цькою**) onto the language's name and you're done.
after: To ask politely: **Ви говорите англійською?** — probably the sentence you'll use most in your first week.
To admit your limits: **Я говорю тільки трохи** (I only speak a little) or **Я ще вивчаю** (I'm still learning).

sections.title: Nationalities: different for men and women

blocks.text: Unlike English, Ukrainian nationality words have two forms. You only need to memorize the one that describes you — the rest will come by ear.

Notice the pattern: the man's form almost always ends in **-ець**, which shrinks to **-ця** in other cases; the woman's form almost always ends in **-ка**. If in doubt, the safe route that's always right is to name the country: *Я з Індонезії* — and that's what people use most anyway.

blocks.title: В Україні, not на Україні
items: To say "in Ukraine", Ukrainian uses **в Україні** — the preposition *в*, as with any country: *в Індонезії*, *в Польщі*, *в Японії*.
The form **на Україні** used to be common in Russian and implies a region, not a country. It was dropped long ago and sounds offensive to many people.
The practical rule is simple: **countries take в, islands and regions take на**. *В Україні*, *в Індонезії*, but *на Балі*, *на Яві*, *на Суматрі*.
⚠️ This is one of the few grammar mistakes in this course that's about more than right and wrong. If you remember just one thing from this page, make it this one.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with з + the correct form of the country.
Fill in the blanks with the correct language form (-ською).
Put the words in the right order.

items: He's from Lviv, but now he lives in Kyiv.
I don't speak Ukrainian yet. Only a little.

answers: з Індонезії — з України — з Польщі — з Японії — з Канади
Звідки ти? — Я з Індонезії. — Я трохи говорю українською. — Я живу в Києві. — Це дуже далеко.
Звідки ти? — Я з Індонезії, з Джакарти. — Він зі Львова, але зараз живе в Києві. — Я ще не говорю українською. Тільки трохи. — Ви говорите англійською?
wave: Review Unit 1. By now *Ласкаво просимо до Києва* should read as "welcome to Kyiv" — and you can see for yourself why the ending is **Києва**, not **Київ**.
